key_insight: In low-dimensional pnictogen chalcohalides, the most stable surface facets can still differ in band-edge positions by up to 0.8 eV, making surface orientation a hidden driver of solar-cell performance.
engineering_relevance: Controlling crystal facet exposure and contact matching could substantially improve charge extraction and open-circuit voltage in MChX photovoltaic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of surface energetics across Bi/Sb chalcogen-halide compounds
Exhaustive sampling of crystal orientations, including low-symmetry facets
Drift-diffusion device simulations for BiSBr to quantify performance impact
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the (011) and (010) facets are most stable across all eight compounds, with only 0.01–0.03 J m^-2 formation-energy differences but up to 0.8 eV band-edge shifts; simulations indicate as much as a 0.6 V Voc loss from facet coexistence.
watch_item: The performance impact is modeled for an idealized, defect-free absorber, so real-device disorder, defects, and interfacial chemistry may change the magnitude of the effect.
paper_title: Surface Physics of Low-Dimensional Pnictogen Chalcohalides and Its Impact on Photovoltaic Technologies
